note: Re-judged (independent auditor) after 0bf856490c retagged the resolver high-bit paragraph to RFC2181-8-2. Section 8: "It is hereby specified that a TTL value is an unsigned number, with a minimum value of 0, and a maximum value of 2147483647." and "When transmitted, this value shall be encoded in the less significant 31 bits of the 32 bit TTL field, with the most significant, or sign, bit set to zero." geodns (unchanged units): TestRFC2181TTLTransmittedWithSignBitClear accepts configured TTL 0 and reads every packed A/NS/SOA TTL field back at default-ttl 2147483647 with the top bit clear; TestRFC2181_TTLSignBitBound positive keeps 2147483647 exactly and its negative refuses 2147483648 at parseTTL, the only source of a configured geodns TTL (default-ttl and per-host ttl). That is a genuine conforming/violating pair over both clauses. Resolver: the 8-1 negative now stands alone in this scope and is a conforming boundary input, not a violating one: a received 2147483647 with max-ttl raised to 2147483647 is answered and re-served from cache unchanged, which catches an off-by-one that treats the maximum as out of range (record: receivedTTL ttl >= ttlSignBit-1 mutant, observed red); it is a second positive in substance, and the row's violating-input negative is the geodns 2147483648 refusal. The resolver's transmit clause is held by receivedTTL's sign-bit check plus min with a limit the YANG bounds to 0..2147483647 (cache max-ttl and max-negative-ttl); a resolver relaying a sign-bit TTL would turn this same unit red through its RFC2181-8-2 assertion (0x80000001 answered as 0), but no 8-1-tagged assertion and no tagged test of the YANG range would, and the 8-2 record's break (false && sign check) leaves 8-1 met because the YANG-bounded cap still clears the bit. Finding recorded, verdict stands on the geodns pair plus the resolver unit.
